abstract.text:
Abstract—To address the issue of static voltage stability in 
distribution networks with high proportion distributed pv 
generation(DG) during fault, this paper establish a fault 
equivalent model which consider the characteristics of PV 
equipment during low -voltage ride -through(LVRT). The 
model derives the constraints on the PV current phase angle 
required to maintain static voltage stability. Subsequently, the 
impact of DG capacity at the point of common coupling and 
the electrical distance between the distribution network and 
the AC power source on the PV output current phase angle 
constraint is quantitatively analyzed. On this basis, a current 
control method is proposed: when there is a voltage stability 
risk in the system, the active and reactive current injection 
from the PV is adjusted, while under no voltage stability risk, 
the low -voltage ride -through control strategy remains 
unaffected. Finally, simulation examples based on the 
Matlab/Simulink testing platform verify the validity of the 
analysis and the proposed control strategy.

introduction.text:
I. INTRODUCTION 
The sustainable development of DG contributes to 
promoting energy conservation , emission reduction , 
achieving sustainable economic and social development  [1]. 
However, the rapid growth of DG is accompanied by 
increased operational risks to distribution networks and 
voltage stability issues arise during low-voltage ride-through 
(LVRT) in certain areas.  Researching the voltage stability 
mechanism and control strategies of DG during LVRT has a 
great significance for improving power quality and supply 
reliability. 
Currently, the main methods which is short circuit ratio 
[2][3], eigenvalue analysis  [4], and impedance margin  [5] is 
used to evaluate the static voltage stability of power systems. 
Reference [6] considers the impact of different power 
growth modes on the static voltage stability of the system . 
This academic proposes the short circuit ratio index for new 
energy station. Reference  [7] establishes a bi -level optimal 
power flow model to determine the static voltage stability 
margin interval , which considering the uncertainty of 
renewable energy stations. Reference [ 8] base s on the 
characteristics of radial distribution systems . Then the 
academic proposes a method a voltage stability analysis 
which is  suitable for distribution networks. Reference [9] 
uses the singularity of the power flow Jacobian matrix at the 
static voltage stability critical point, and describes this 
characteristic by setting the determinant of the Jacobian to 
zero [10]. 
During LVRT, the output current of DG is “Both 
magnitude and phase are constrained.” Once integrated into 
distribution networks, the traditional short circuit ratio and 
impedance margin methods cannot fully consider the 
characteristics of PV devices  [12], which makes it difficult to 
define a clear boundary value for the corresponding results  
[13]. The eigenvalue evaluation method requires computing 
the eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix, which entails 
substantial computational effort and low online calculation 
efficiency, making it unsuitable for online stability control 
applications [14]. Stability control based on constructing 
dynamic compensation control loops is more readily 
implemented which apply on a large number of DG in 
distribution networks  [15]. Current research mainly focuses 
on transient stability of power angle and frequency, while 
research on this aspect is relatively limited [16]. 
This paper analyzes the static voltage stability 
mechanism of DG during LVRT, and derives the range of 
DG current output angles that ensure voltage stability in the 
distribution network. Based on this, the paper further 
examines the influence of DG’s capacity and the electrical 
distance ,which is between distribution network and AC 
power sources , on the range of PV output current angles. 
Subsequently, the critical current value for voltage stability is 
derived, and a current critical value calculation module is 
designed. When the classic LVRT strategy of DG would 
otherwise lead to voltage instability, the current calculation 
module adjusts the DG output current dynamically. Finally, 
simulation cases built in MATLAB/Simulink are used to 
verify the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

conclusion.text:
V. CONCLUSION 
To address the problem of system voltage instability 
caused by photovoltaic current injection during faults, this 
paper proposes a static voltage stability analysis and control 
strategy for distribution networks during faults. The 
following conclusions are obtained through simulation 
verification: 
(1) The large access capacity of distributed photovoltaic 
power and the long electrical distance between the 
distribution network and the AC power supply are the main 
factors leading to static voltage instability during faults. 
(2) The strategy proposed in this paper calculates the 
output Angle range of the photovoltaic current under the 
condition of voltage stability during the fault period, and 
then corrects the current reference value of the low -
penetration strategy, which can effectively improve the static 
voltage stability during the fault ride-through period. 
Compared with the classic low -voltage ride -through 
control strategy, the strategy proposed in this paper has a 
smaller computational load and does not require significant 
modifications to the photovoltaic control structure, thus 
having stronger applicability.
